title: Jude and the Ledger
premise: In the winter of the great storms, Quentin Okonkwo keeps the light at Gullwrack Point alone, her grief and her ledgers the only company she allows. When a stranger named Jude washes ashore carrying letters in the unmistakable hand of her husband Emeric—declared dead three years ago—Quentin's careful solitude shatters. As the storms close the harbor and a rescue ship offers only one last berth, Jude's true identity surfaces: he is Emeric's brother, and the letters are bait to draw Quentin into a smuggling ring Emeric faked his death to escape. In the final storm, Quentin must choose who takes the berth—Jude, the found family she never wanted, or herself—and she gives it away, staying to keep the light, only for Emeric himself to climb the tower at dawn, alive, asking to be remembered.
about_author: Xanthe Thornbury is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maritime correspondence from coastal lighthouse stations before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted signal house on the northern coast, where she collects tide tables and unfinished letters.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ink
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Establishes her routines at Gullwrack Point: trimming wicks, logging weather, rereading Emeric's last letter. She has stopped writing entries about herself in the ledger. Emotional beat: grief disguised as diligence.

chapters.title: A Body of Water
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The first great storm hits; she spots something in the surf and drags an unconscious stranger inside. He clutches an oilskin packet to his chest even while half-drowned. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion breaking routine.

chapters.title: Handwriting
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. He wakes disoriented, hides his purpose, and watches Quentin discover the packet's letters—in Emeric's hand, dated after his death. Her face goes white. Emotional beat: the ground opening under a settled life.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Keeps
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She interrogates the letters against her own memory of Emeric's penmanship, finding details only he could know—including a private joke about her freckles. Emotional beat: hope arriving as an intruder.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wouldn't Say His Name
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Quentin demands answers; Jude gives a false name and a half-true story of shipwreck. Their wary cohabitation begins—he mends nets, she pretends not to notice. Emotional beat: two liars circling politely.

chapters.title: Salt and Bread
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A small domestic scene: shared meals, repaired shutters, Jude teaching her a card game Emeric loved. She catches herself laughing and hates it. Emotional beat: found family taking root uninvited.

chapters.title: The Harbormaster's Summons
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Word comes that the relief ship Meridian will make one final run before the harbor freezes—one berth for evacuation. Quentin realizes she and Jude cannot both leave. Emotional beat: the choice taking shape.

chapters.title: Letters Not Sent
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Alone in the tower, Jude reads more of the packet and we learn the truth: he is Emeric's younger brother, sent by the smuggling ring to confirm Emeric's death—or expose it. Emotional beat: guilt compounding deception.

chapters.title: The Third Letter
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She finds a letter addressed to her by name, hidden deeper in the packet, warning: 'Trust no one who brings my hand to you.' She confronts Jude with a lantern and a knife. Emotional beat: trust fracturing.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude admits who he is—not why the letters exist. Quentin throws him out into the wind; he refuses to go, standing watch in the boathouse all night. Emotional beat: anger that cannot quite become hatred.

chapters.title: The Ring Comes Ashore
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Two strangers arrive claiming to be salvagers, asking pointed questions about 'papers' washed up. Quentin lies smoothly and understands Emeric faked his death to escape them. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What Emeric Was Running From
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude tells Quentin everything: the smuggling ledger, the drowned informant, Emeric's staged wreck. The letters were meant to lure Quentin out as leverage. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as protection gone wrong.

chapters.title: The Berth
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The Meridian signals its approach; the harbormaster confirms one seat. Quentin quietly begins deciding between Jude—who has become family—and herself, keeper of a light no one else can tend. Emotional beat: love measured in sacrifice.

chapters.title: Storm Glass Falling
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Barometer plunging; the worst storm in living memory builds. Quentin and Jude work together battening the tower, their old wariness burned off by shared labor. Emotional beat: partnership forged under pressure.

chapters.title: The Salvagers Return
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The two strangers return armed, demanding the letters, holding Jude at gunpoint on the gallery. Quentin douses the light—a keeper's ultimate transgression—to plunge the rocks into darkness. Emotional beat: defiance at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Blackout
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In darkness and screaming wind, Jude fights one salvager over the gallery rail; the other flees into the storm. Jude is wounded; Quentin relights the lamp with shaking hands. Emotional beat: terror and tenderness entwined.

chapters.title: The Ship That Shouldn't Be There
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Through the storm's eye, Quentin sees a small boat running the rocks toward shore—steered by a man with Emeric's stance, coming back for the letters, or for her. Emotional beat: the dead walking out of the sea.

chapters.title: Emeric
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Emeric arrives soaked and hollow, confessing the fake death, the ring, the letters he never wrote—Jude forged them from memory to draw the ring's hunters away from his brother. Emotional beat: reunion as reckoning, not comfort.

chapters.title: Three at the Rail
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The Meridian's longboat waits through the last window before the harbor closes. One berth. Emeric insists Jude take it; Jude refuses; Quentin ends the argument by naming herself keeper to the end. Emotional beat: each trying to be the one left behind.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin puts Jude aboard—the brother who chose honesty, the family she found—giving him the letters as evidence to end the ring. Emeric stays, bound to the light and to her judgment. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship of one's own story.

chapters.title: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: Quentin and Emeric's alternating POV. They keep the light together through the storm's final fury, working in wordless rhythm like the marriage they once had, saying nothing that can't be unsaid. Emotional beat: endurance as forgiveness in progress.

chapters.title: New Entries
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Spring. The ring broken by Jude's testimony, a letter arrives from him—alive, settled, calling her family. Quentin opens a fresh ledger and writes both names in it: hers and Emeric's, side by side, beginning again. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, memory kept, light still burning.
